correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact all-n proof: below a triple-marker factor, two-marker windows recover every gap below k−1; one-marker multiplicities simplify by inclusion–exclusion because two short neighboring gaps would force a third gap larger than the maximum; zero-only windows use the total zero count. At the first triple-marker read the oriented gap cycle is fixed. Constructive spectrum-equivalent competitor triples show every lower bound, while integer compositions and uniform-simplex lattice limits give exact T_n(k), the worst-case threshold and the limiting moments. Boundary n=3,4 separately handled. Independent direct-string program exhaustively checked 23,751 three-one words, 1,098 necklaces, 23,841 spectra through n=28 and rational moment integration; all passed. Finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The classical Ukkonen/Pevzner condition and the Bresler–Bresler–Tse (2013) de Bruijn/Eulerian uniqueness treatment cover qualitative reconstruction for general strings. They are credited rather than claimed new. The inspected full 2013 reconstruction article contains no closed three-one necklace threshold distribution or probability law. The quantitative theorem here includes a five-case individual gap formula, all-length exact threshold counts, precise two/four extremizer numbers, and a nondegenerate Dirichlet limit with rational moments. These do not follow as stated from the generic reconstruction criterion without the new gap case analysis and lattice counting. Karhumäki–Saarela–Zamboni define linear k-Abelian equivalence but do not enumerate the present circular sparse-read spectra. A genuinely equivalent unindexed specialization remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Classical general uniqueness criteria imply an algorithmic solution for each given input; originality must be attributed to the explicit closed distribution and limiting law, not mere decision of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The natural noisy-free sparse circular-genome model asks for the minimum length of complete exact reads needed for unique reconstruction. The result fully determines this for every three-one circle and every length, not just a small table. It pinpoints orientation ambiguity when all three zero gaps differ, gives a sharp family-wide 2n/3 worst case with only 2 or 4 extremizers, and obtains the exact entire threshold distribution plus a nondegenerate broken-stick limit with mean 7/18 and variance 13/648. These quantitative structural population results are not routine reindexings of a single run or arbitrary finite cutoffs; they go beyond the algorithmic fact that a generic de Bruijn graph can test uniqueness.
